I'll start by examining the repository and the failing tests.The root cause is clear: `parse_variables` guards the final literal yield with `if False:`, so all text after the last placeholder — and entire strings with no placeholders — is discarded. Fixing it restores all three failing tests.All 9 acceptance tests pass.

## Change summary

**File:** `dotenv/variables.py`

**Cause:** In `parse_variables`, the trailing-literal emission was dead code guarded by `if False:`. As a result:
- strings with no placeholders (e.g. `"literal"`, `"new"`, `"one"`) yielded no atoms and resolved to `""`;
- text after the last `${...}` placeholder (e.g. `"-post"`) was dropped.

This explains the observed failures in `test_trailing`, `test_override`, and `test_interpolation` (the latter failed because `A=one` was itself truncated to `""`, so `B=${A}` resolved to `""`).

**Fix:** Replace the `if False:` guard with the correct condition `if cursor < length:`, yielding the remaining literal text only when non-empty. This preserves existing behavior (no empty trailing `Literal`) while restoring complete text preservation.

Verification: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` → 9 tests, OK.
